draft.title: Why scientists classify living things
card: Scientists have found millions of kinds of living things, and many more are still unnamed. Classifying means sorting them into groups by shared features.
Identify: a group with known features helps us work out what an unknown organism is. If it has feathers and a beak, it belongs with the birds.
Study: organisms in the same group often share other features, so learning about one can help scientists predict things about others in that group.
Talk: group names give scientists a shared way to describe living things, so they can compare their findings clearly.
draft.remember: Classifying sorts life by shared features, so it is easier to identify, study and discuss.

a.q: Why do scientists put living things into groups based on features they share?
opts: It makes the variety of life easier to identify and study
It lets them rank living things from least to most important
It shows which living things are the most useful to humans
It means each living thing needs only one group name
a.why: Groups with known features let scientists work out what an organism is and compare it with others. Sorting does not rank organisms by importance, because groups are based on shared features, not on value.
a.clue: Think about what groups help scientists do with unknown organisms.

b.q: Priya finds an unknown insect in a park in Melbourne. It has six legs and three body parts. How does classification help her work out what it is?
opts: She can match its features to a known group to identify it
She can tell how long the insect will live from its colour
She can be sure that no one has seen this insect before
She can name the insect by choosing any word she likes
b.why: Classification groups organisms by shared features, so Priya can compare the insect's features with known groups and narrow down what it is. Its features cannot show that it is new, because many known insects share them.
b.clue: Her insect has features she can compare with groups.

a.best: It makes the variety of life easier to identify and study

b.best: She can match its features to a known group to identify it
